Root.overflowEdgeThreshold.semantic: pixels that must be passed before the overflow edge data attributes (data-overflow-x-start etc.) are applied; a single number applies to all edges — used to avoid flicker on tiny overflows and to drive scroll fade masks.

Root CSS variables.semantic: measured corner size, for sizing/positioning a custom corner.

Viewport.semantic: the actual native scroll container (overflow:auto element); must wrap Content; focusable by default because it is keyboard-scrollable.

Scrollbar.orientation.semantic: which axis this scrollbar controls; render two for both axes and add Corner.

Scrollbar.keepMounted.semantic: keep the scrollbar element in the DOM when the viewport is not scrollable (otherwise it unmounts).

Content.semantic: content wrapper inside the Viewport; carries the same overflow/scroll data attributes.

Thumb.semantic: the draggable indicator; sized/positioned by the component, style width/height to taste.

Corner.semantic: rectangular filler at the intersection of two scrollbars; required when both axes are present.

dataAttributes: Root / Viewport / Content: data-scrolling, data-has-overflow-x, data-has-overflow-y, data-overflow-x-start, data-overflow-x-end, data-overflow-y-start, data-overflow-y-end

Scrollbar: data-orientation, data-hovering (pointer over the scroll area), data-scrolling, data-has-overflow-x, data-has-overflow-y, data-overflow-x-start, data-overflow-x-end, data-overflow-y-start, data-overflow-y-end
renderProp: Shared `render` contract (ReactElement | (props, state) => ReactElement) on all six parts plus state-driven className/style; documented advanced usage composes ScrollArea.Viewport into another component's render prop: <Tabs.List render={<ScrollArea.Viewport/>}/>. Custom primitives: useRender; merging: mergeProps/mergePropsN.
controlled: None — the scroll area is uncontrolled by design (scroll position lives in the DOM). There are no value/defaultValue/open props and no change callbacks; consumers observe state through data-* attributes and can drive the viewport imperatively via its DOM element.
keyboard: No keyboard handling of its own: Base UI ScrollArea keeps a NATIVE scroll container (the Viewport), so keyboard scrolling (arrows/Page/Home/End when the viewport is focused), wheel, touch and scrollbar drag all come from the browser. There is no ARIA scrollbar widget, no arrow-key stepping and no PageUp/PageDown code anywhere in the package (verified by searching the compiled sources). Visibility of custom scrollbars is CSS-driven: the docs style them with data-hovering / data-scrolling (scrollbars are opacity 0 + pointer-events:none until hovering/scrolling).
notableDifferences: React Aria has no ScrollArea primitive; the closest migration target is a plain overflow container. Base UI adds: custom Scrollbar/Thumb/Corner parts, cross-axis overflow data attributes for fade masks, and a `data-hovering`/`data-scrolling` visibility contract — but scrolling itself stays native, so no `type='scroll'|'hover'` behaviour modes and no programmatic scroll API are provided.
All show/hide logic is delegated to CSS via data attributes (no shadow DOM, no JS opacity), and `keepMounted` on the Scrollbar is the only mounting control.
Two scrollbars require two explicit <ScrollArea.Scrollbar> elements (one with orientation='horizontal') plus <ScrollArea.Corner/> to keep them from intersecting.
Overflow detection is configurable through `overflowEdgeThreshold` (default 0) so small overflow deltas do not toggle the edge attributes/fades.
